newsitem.title: USA: U.S. High Court denies Florida prison term appeal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. High Court denies Florida prison term appeal.

text.p: The Supreme Court Tuesday denied Florida's appeal of a ruling that requires it to provide early release for good behaviour to more than 20,000 inmates convicted of violent crimes and sex offences.
The justices let stand a Florida Supreme Court decision in October that the state could not retroactively mandate that prisoners serve 85 percent of their sentences.

The state high court ruled unanimously that the Florida Department of Corrections could not expand a 1995 law requiring that inmates serve at least 85 percent of their sentence to prisoners who were already incarcerated at the time.

Changing the rules after the prisoners had already received their sentences violated their constitutional rights, the state court said. The decision affected an estimated one-third of the state's prison population.

Faced with overcrowded prisons, Florida previously had employed generous early release terms as an incentive for following prison rules. Prisoners could be credited with as much as 20 days off each month for good behaviour.

Florida Attorney General Robert Butterworth appealed to the Supreme Court, asking the justices to "quash" the state court decision. But the high court denied his appeal without any comment or dissent.

The case involved Richard Gwong, who is serving a 22-year sentence for murder. He was sentenced in 1989. The state had complained that his sentence could be cut by as much as one- third due to time off for good behaviour.
